rationale: The primary account rests on the removal guard firing because the local Progress entry disappears. Its remaining source-derived boundary was that transitions which keep the member in a configuration half leave the gate armed, and this is exactly what a positive control can settle: a joint-explicit removal that is never left keeps the member as an outgoing voter, so if the gate stays armed its proposals must be accepted and committed while every other condition of the witness scenario is unchanged apart from the missing removal from both halves.

investigations.question: Does the held-proposal effect require the committed configuration change to drop the local member from both halves of the configuration, so that a member that remains a participant (for example an outgoing voter of a joint configuration that is never left) keeps its proposal gate armed and reaches a decision normally?
investigations.hypothesis: The node.run() removal guard is guarded by the disappearance of the local Progress entry, which LeaveJoint performs for outgoing voters that are in neither the incoming half nor the learner set, while EnterJoint keeps the entry for outgoing voters. A member that stays an outgoing voter therefore keeps the gate armed and its proposals are forwarded and committed.
investigations.discriminator: Run the same three-node Node-API cluster, elect leader 1, propose a joint-explicit removal of node 3 that is never left (so node 3 stays an outgoing voter), then invoke Propose on node 3 while it is still a participant and record whether the call returns and whether its payload commits, in contrast to the witness scenario where the member is dropped from both halves and the same invocation does not complete.

scope.description: Three real raft nodes (ids 1,2,3) driven through the async Node API in one process. Node 1 campaigns and becomes leader at term 1 in the configuration {1,2,3}; a ConfChangeV2 with Transition JointExplicit and a single remove change for node 3 is proposed on node 1, which enters a joint configuration that is never left. The harness waits until node 3's own configuration lists it in the outgoing half, records that membership, then invokes Node.Propose on node 3 and records whether the call returns, with which error, how long it took, and whether its payload reaches any node's committed entries.
assumptions: Reliable, per-sender ordered in-process delivery; no ticks are delivered, so leader 1 stays in place.
The joint state is not left because the proposal uses the explicit transition and the harness never proposes the empty leave change.
Node 3 applies the joint change through Node.ApplyConfChange as the driver consumes its Ready, so its own view of the joint membership is the one observed.
excluded: Removal from both halves (covered by the witness scenario in the parent investigation)
RawNode.Propose, async storage writes, message loss and ticks

experiment.prefix: Start nodes 1,2,3 with a MemoryStorage per node whose ConfState voters are {1,2,3}. Node 1 campaigns at term 1 and becomes leader; every node then reports leader 1 and node 1 has applied the initial entry. Propose on node 1 a ConfChangeV2 with Transition JointExplicit carrying remove node 3 and wait until node 3's own configuration lists it in the outgoing half while still counting it as a voter. Then invoke Node.Propose on node 3 with a bounded context and record the returned error, elapsed time and the membership at that moment, followed by a bounded scan for the payload in every node's committed entries.
experiment.responsibility: Client-facing obligation of the Node interface: a Propose invocation on a member that is still a participant of the active configuration must reach a proposal outcome, while the same invocation on a member dropped from both halves must not be silently held.

comparisons.description: While the member is an outgoing voter of a joint configuration that is never left, its invocation returned instead of staying pending.
That invocation's payload was committed, so the member's proposal duty was completed rather than dropped.
